nodes.author: Verkruysse et al.
nodes.norm_label: verkruysse et al. 2008 (remote ppg green channel)

nodes.label: Wang et al. 2017 - Algorithmic Principles of Remote PPG (POS)
nodes.author: Wang et al.
nodes.norm_label: wang et al. 2017 - algorithmic principles of remote ppg (pos)

nodes.label: synthetic_unvalidated baseline.joblib classifier
nodes.rationale: Trained on synthetic signal features because no labeled real/fake video dataset was provided; marked synthetic_unvalidated and excluded from the live rPPG decision.

nodes.label: CHROM rPPG method
nodes.rationale: Projects RGB onto two chrominance axes designed to cancel specular reflection and illumination-driven intensity changes, then combines using their std-dev ratio to suppress remaining motion.

nodes.label: Green rPPG method
nodes.rationale: Haemoglobin absorbs green light most strongly so the raw green channel carries the strongest plethysmographic AC component - simplest and most replicated, but most motion-sensitive.

nodes.label: POS rPPG method (default)
nodes.rationale: Projects temporally-normalised RGB onto the plane orthogonal to the assumed skin-tone/illumination vector over a sliding ~1.6s window; tends to generalise better across skin tones and lighting than CHROM, so it is the default method.

nodes.label: Shared rPPG preprocessing chain
nodes.rationale: All three methods share smoothness-priors detrending, z-score normalisation and a Butterworth band-pass restricted to 0.7-4.0 Hz (42-240 BPM) so downstream comparison is apples-to-apples.

nodes.label: Model-free rPPG decision
nodes.rationale: The live verdict is built only from measured rPPG cues; missing temporal or morphology measurements are neutral rather than silently treated as evidence of a natural pulse, and the optional synthetic classifier is never loaded or used.

nodes.label: Amplitude consistency feature (amplitude_cv)
nodes.rationale: Coefficient of variation of peak spectral amplitude across regions - real blood flow scales roughly proportionally across the face.

nodes.label: CLAHE dark-frame contrast enhancement
nodes.rationale: Enhancement is now used only to help face detection, never to derive the measured signal - an early bug applied contrast correction to the same frame later used for RGB measurement, corrupting the small pulsatile amplitude.

nodes.label: Cross-region physiological consistency
nodes.rationale: Real facial blood flow pulses near-synchronously across forehead and both cheeks, so pairwise Pearson correlation plus 0.15 Hz dominant-frequency agreement test physiological coherence - low agreement is evidence against a coherent signal but not proof of manipulation, which is why motion and illumination are surfaced as separate confounds.

nodes.label: Harmonic ratio feature
nodes.rationale: Real pulse waveforms are not pure sinusoids so energy should appear at 2x and 3x the dominant cardiac frequency - but on pure noise the ratio can score higher than on a real signal, so it is mitigated by signal-quality gating rather than fixed at the source.

nodes.label: Phase coherence feature
nodes.rationale: Cross-region phase stability via the Hilbert transform, verified by testing to separate synchronised synthetic signals (coherence > 0.8) from pure noise (coherence < 0.3).

nodes.label: SNR-based signal quality score
nodes.rationale: Welch PSD power within +/-0.1 Hz of the dominant peak and its first harmonic maps to a 0-100 score via a clipped linear scale (-10dB to 0, +12dB to 100) - a documented heuristic, not a clinically validated scale.

nodes.label: Harmonic ratio unreliable without a real dominant peak
nodes.norm_label: harmonic ratio unreliable without a real dominant peak
nodes.rationale: 'Energy near 2x/3x the peak' is only meaningful when the peak is a real cardiac frequency; on pure noise the ratio can score higher than on a real signal. Neutralised by signal-quality gating rather than fixed at the source.

nodes.label: Motion, lighting and compression sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Green/CHROM/POS are all sensitive to head motion, illumination change and heavy compression regardless of whether the video is real or fake, which is why warnings explicitly separate 'reasons this measurement might be unreliable' from evidence for/against authenticity.

nodes.label: Three-process architecture (web / api / ml)
nodes.rationale: The split exists so the computationally/scientifically hard part (rPPG extraction) can be developed, tested, and iterated on entirely independently of the web application shell.

nodes.label: Analysis sub-resource endpoints (signal, features, report, visuals)
nodes.norm_label: analysis sub-resource endpoints (signal, features, report, visuals)

nodes.label: Pipeline tab visualization trace
nodes.rationale: FrameTraceCollector samples a normalised per-frame trace at ~5 Hz bounded to 600 entries and the file is written in a finally block, so even failed analyses show how far they got.

nodes.label: Data storage decisions
nodes.rationale: Raw video lives on disk never in the database; results are a single JSON-encoded text column because SQLite has no native Json type; large arrays are externalized to artifact files; all storage paths resolve against the repo root by walking up to pnpm-workspace.yaml.

nodes.label: Video upload to result request flow
nodes.norm_label: video upload to result request flow

nodes.label: Haar cascade face detector fallback
nodes.rationale: Ships bundled inside opencv-python so it requires no network download, making it the one face-detection path fully testable in a network-restricted environment during development.

nodes.label: MediaPipe face detection dependency and fail-closed behaviour
nodes.norm_label: mediapipe face detection dependency and fail-closed behaviour
nodes.rationale: MediaPipe Face Landmarker needs a downloaded .task model file; videos with no detectable face fail closed with 'no usable signal' rather than a wrong prediction, but coverage on low-quality footage is inherently limited.

nodes.label: Codebase generation environment constraints
nodes.rationale: The scientific core was written and tested end-to-end with NumPy/SciPy/OpenCV/MediaPipe/scikit-learn, while the Node/Express API and React frontend could not be npm-installed or run in the generation environment (no network), so the first local run is where integration bugs are most likely to surface.

nodes.label: StratifiedGroupKFold training protocol
nodes.rationale: StratifiedGroupKFold on subject ID, not plain K-fold, is required for a valid subject-independent evaluation - a model that has seen a person's face in training will look artificially good on a different clip of the same person at test time.

nodes.label: Not implemented / explicitly out of scope
nodes.norm_label: not implemented / explicitly out of scope

nodes.label: No validated real-video accuracy
nodes.rationale: The 94% accuracy and 0.982 AUC are from a random holdout of the same synthetic signal generator; they do not measure accuracy on genuine or deepfake videos and no cross-dataset test has been run.

nodes.label: ML service internal endpoints (services/ml)
nodes.rationale: Internal only, called by apps/api; POST /v1/analyse runs the full pipeline while POST /v1/inference runs only the classifier on a precomputed feature dict.

nodes.label: apps/api Express service
nodes.rationale: Owns video storage bookkeeping, the analysis queue, the SQLite schema and WebSocket progress events, but contains zero OpenCV/ML code - its only contact with the science is a single HTTP client (python.service.ts).

nodes.label: services/ml FastAPI ML service
nodes.rationale: Stateless: given a video path and parameters it returns structured JSON, owning 100% of video processing, rPPG extraction, feature engineering and cue fusion, and knows nothing about SQLite or HTTP sessions.

nodes.label: Polling-based progress reporting
nodes.rationale: POST /v1/analyse is a single blocking call, so the Node side polls the ML progress registry every 700ms; this keeps the transport simple (plain HTTP, no SSE/WebSocket fan-in between services) while still driving the per-stage progress bar. ProgressCallback in end_to_end.py is the seam if streaming is ever wanted.

nodes.label: apps/web React SPA
nodes.rationale: Contains zero signal-processing logic; it only ever displays what the API returns.

nodes.label: Single-process WebSocket fan-out
nodes.rationale: The queue runs in the same process as the HTTP server so emitAnalysisEvent always reaches every connected browser with no cross-process adapter - a deliberate consequence of zero-infra mode; a multi-instance deployment would need socket.io-redis plus an external queue.

nodes.label: In-process analysis queue (analysis.queue.ts)
nodes.rationale: Concurrency 2 with retry and exponential backoff (up to 3 retries, 5s backoff) keeps the local stack zero-infra; BullMQ/Redis were removed.

nodes.label: Zero-infra local mode (SQLite + in-process queue)
nodes.rationale: SQLite plus an in-process job queue means no Docker, Postgres or Redis is required to run the full stack locally.

nodes.label: Confidence discounting by measurement strength
nodes.rationale: Reports the rPPG cue score after discounting it by measurement strength - a heuristic score, not a calibrated probability of authenticity.

nodes.label: Evidence and warning generation
nodes.rationale: Converts computed features into plain-language evidence and warning strings using fixed, documented thresholds (not learned), e.g. signal quality below 40 always produces an unreliability warning.

nodes.label: Signal-quality gating is a heuristic
nodes.rationale: The SNR-to-quality mapping and the confidence-discounting curve are heuristics, not fitted to labelled ground truth (e.g. Platt scaling), so they must be calibrated against a verified video benchmark before being read as probabilities.
